grounding.quote:
They are conditions of the work this family governs, not
commitments, and do not follow from finite capacity alone. Two of P0's
premises are cited by name: its actor-change premise, that the actor of one
step need not be the actor of the next and may re-acquire declared sources
but not private memory; and its open-world premise, that the world is open.
The standing of the consequences below is stated in
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law).

concepts.label: F1 frames-and-context foundation table
concepts.definition: Family F1, frames and context, traces bounded-frame engagement across this member, ACTIVATION §2 and FOUNDATIONS §2 frame objects, authorities, independence and tuple. The table owns none of the rules it names. Instance premises are workspace material exceeding one actor's competence/context/tools/access; declared outcome questions; possibly overlapping frames/actors; changing workspace/topology/capabilities; and actor use of owning and derived sources. These are work conditions, not foundational commitments or consequences of finite capacity alone. P0 is recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 are cited as independent; P4b is derived from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step facts; P5 is derived from P0/P6 with the open-world premise. P0 also includes actor change with declared-source reacquisition rather than private memory. Rows distinguish consequences, owning rules, additional choices/owners and pillars; RF-012 and result mappings are traced in F3, imports in F12. Core claims and violation lists add no independent rules.

grounding.quote: coverage is evaluated against an exact tuple of workspace, governed outcome, basis, evaluation inventory, frame set and time, and a change of any material member may invalidate it.

concepts.label: Frame coverage audit
concepts.definition: Coverage is an audit relative to an exact workspace, governed outcome, basis, evaluation inventory, frame set and time. Its ledger and statuses concern coverage predicates and are distinct from results of the covered evaluations. Operational full coverage remains relative to that tuple and an explicit residual boundary.

grounding.quote:
Every performed evaluation of a frame returns one closed result in the
frame's declared result algebra: the core algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), or a refinement mapped
into it under that section. That section owns the five core values
(`satisfied`, `falsified`, `indeterminate`, `out_of_frame` and
`invalid_basis`), their meanings and the rules over them: that nothing is
coerced to success; that a refinement adds no core value, keeps
indeterminate, out-of-frame and invalid-basis pressure explicit and raises
no result's standing; and that an evaluation not performed has no result,
its stop state being
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition). This law
applies them to every frame and defines none of them (P5).

concepts.label: Frame result domain
concepts.definition: A frame evaluation returns one closed result in its declared algebra: the FOUNDATIONS §4 core values satisfied, falsified, indeterminate, out_of_frame and invalid_basis, or a refinement mapped into that algebra. The owning core meanings and standing are imported, not redefined by REFERENCE_FRAME.
conditions: Evaluation is performed.
exceptions: An evaluation not performed has no evaluation result; its stop state belongs to ACTIVATION §3.

grounding.quote:
A reference frame is atomic at engagement altitude: it is activated and
evaluated as one bounded attention unit. Semantic irreducibility is a
separate question: one frame may contain several semantic atoms, and one
semantic atom may take part in several frames (P1, P3). Where an adopting
method supplies a semantic-contraction law for its domain atoms, that law
governs the domain atom family.

concepts.label: Semantic atom
concepts.definition: A semantic atom concerns irreducible meaning; an engagement atom concerns one bounded activation/evaluation. One frame may contain several semantic atoms and one semantic atom may participate in several frames. An adopting domain method's semantic-contraction law governs its domain atom family, not frame-set contraction by default.

grounding.quote:
# Frame: <stable local identity>

## Evaluation Family
<questions, predicates, and closed result algebra>

## Subject And Basis
<workspace boundary, exact identity, version/time/topology coordinates>

concepts.label: Reference frame
concepts.definition: A declared bounded evaluation family with stable local identity; subject and exact basis; material manifold; coordinates and equality; invariants; authorities; admissible evidence; capability envelope; boundaries; optional relations actually used; invalidation and recharting conditions; and qualification cases, counterexamples and residuals.

grounding.quote:
## Evaluation Inventory
<known material evaluations and provenance>

## Selected Frames
<frame identities, revisions, and capability envelopes>

concepts.label: Frame set
concepts.definition: A stable locally identified declaration of governed workspace, outcome, basis and time; human declaration and acceptance authority; known evaluation inventory and provenance; selected frame identities, revisions and capability envelopes; coverage mapping; intentional overlap; required conjunction and translation; residual uncertainty; and revision triggers.

grounding.quote:
The frame and the functions over it remain distinct. An application may
realise the following relations in any conforming form; the signatures
describe relations, not callable software interfaces (P2; RF-016):

concepts.label: Method functions
concepts.definition: Relations distinct from the frame: declare(human_authority, workspace, outcome, practices, capabilities) → frame_set; activate(frame, evaluation, subject, basis, actor) → activated_frame | activation_refusal; evaluate(activated_frame, admissible_evidence) → result + evidence + residuals; conjoin(decision_rule, frame_results) → decision | conflict | indeterminate; translate(source_frame, target_frame, value_or_evidence, mapping) → translated_value | declared_loss | refusal; audit_coverage(workspace, outcome, evaluation_inventory, frame_set) → coverage_ledger; revise(frame_set, new_evidence, failures, capability_change, topology_change) → proposed_frame_set_delta. Later text additionally specifies direct core-value returns absent from the signatures.

grounding.quote:
Frames act together through four distinct relations, and only where the
evaluation requires one (P4a; RF-010).

concepts.label: Frames acting together
concepts.definition: Frames act together through four distinct relations: independently activated co-evaluation, result conjunction, evidence or coordinate translation, and material composition.
conditions: An evaluation requires the relation.

grounding.quote:
Several frames may evaluate the same subject through separate activations
and return closed results. They may overlap in subject, manifold or
evidence sources; neither evaluation consumes or influences the other's
unclosed working result. This serves assurance independence, different
evidence altitudes and distinct failure perspectives (P6; FOUNDATIONS §2,
evaluation independence).

concepts.label: Independently activated co-evaluation
concepts.definition: Several frames may separately activate on the same subject and return closed results, serving assurance independence, different evidence altitudes and distinct failure perspectives.

grounding.quote:
A declared decision rule consumes the closed results of several frames.
The rule, what it must state, and the conjunction it computes are
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
over the core values of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results);
this member defines no conjunction of its own. The outcomes of `conjoin`
map to the core as §5 states (P4a, P5, P6).

concepts.label: Result conjunction
concepts.definition: A declared decision rule consumes several frames' closed results using the core conjunction and rule requirements owned by FOUNDATIONS §4. REFERENCE_FRAME defines no separate conjunction.

grounding.quote:
One frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another. The
translation declares source and target coordinates, preserved meaning,
accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions (P1, P4b).

concepts.label: Evidence or coordinate translation
concepts.definition: One frame supplies evidence or a value consumed inside another through a translation declaring source and target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions.

grounding.quote:
Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning
relation. The owning application declares the composition, the shared
invariants, the effect or decision order where material, closure, failure,
and the conservation of semantic, operation and decision authority.
Composition is introduced only when the evaluation requires it; a possible
future interaction does not require a general composition law in every
frame (P4a, P6, P2).

concepts.label: Material composition
concepts.definition: Several frame-governed operations form one material execution or reasoning relation, declared by the owning application with shared invariants, material effect or decision order, closure, failure and conservation of semantic, operation and decision authority.
conditions: The evaluation requires composition.

grounding.quote:
- governing and subordinate: one frame inherits declared constraints from
  another where a real authority or decomposition relation exists.

concepts.label: Frame relation categories
concepts.definition: Permitted relation categories: disjoint means no shared material variable, coordinate, evidence or result dependency for the declared evaluations; overlapping shares material variables, evidence or entities; complementary jointly informs one decision through distinct evaluations; alternative evaluates the same claim under declared capability or evidence conditions; refinement resolves a distinction another frame aggregates; restriction evaluates a lawful subset of another domain; translated moves values or evidence through a declared coordinate map; temporally successive evaluates a changed basis later; composed combines frame relations into one governed evaluation or action; governing/subordinate inherits declared constraints where real authority or decomposition exists.

grounding.quote:
Coverage is evaluated against the tuple Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T): the
workspace W, the governed outcome G, the exact basis B, the known
evaluation inventory E, the declared frame set S and the time or immutable
checkpoint T of the claim.

concepts.label: Coverage basis
concepts.definition: Coverage(W, G, B, E, S, T): workspace W, governed outcome G, exact basis B, known evaluation inventory E, declared frame set S, and the claim's time or immutable checkpoint T.

grounding.quote:
The coverage evaluator derives the known evaluation inventory from every
material available source, including where applicable:

concepts.label: Evaluation inventory
concepts.definition: Known material evaluations derived by the coverage evaluator from every material available source, recording provenance and materiality.

grounding.quote:
These are lenses (FOUNDATIONS §2): they become frames only when separately
instantiated as bounded evaluation families (P2).

concepts.label: Coverage dimensions
concepts.definition: Cross-cutting audit lenses, typically outcome/capability, identity/authority, lifecycle/temporal behaviour, topology/interactions, transport/representation, evidence/proof, change/failure/recovery/rollback, historical regression, and actor capability/context fit. A lens becomes a frame only through separate instantiation as a bounded evaluation family.

grounding.quote:
whether a row's coverage obligation is met, for the predicate "on the
declared coverage tuple, a capable frame of S covers the evaluation with
no unresolved conflict among the frames, results or authorities that
cover it, or a governing authority the row cites excludes it". Each status
maps to exactly one core value, and the value travels with that predicate
and with the status, whose meaning stays here (P5, P6):

concepts.label: Coverage ledger
concepts.definition: Per-evaluation ledger of coverage obligations. Baseline statuses are covered, separately_covered, conditionally_covered, conflicted, uncovered, unknown and excluded_by_authority. Their predicate is coverage by a capable frame of S on the declared tuple without unresolved conflict among covering frames, results or authorities, or exclusion by the governing authority cited by the row.

grounding.quote:
1. Was the correct declared frame activated?
2. Were the subject and basis exact?
3. Was the actor inside the capability envelope?
4. Was admissible evidence available?
5. Is a material variable or invariant missing from the frame?
6. Is a required conjunction or translation missing?
7. Is the evaluation family itself wrong or incomplete?
8. Is another frame required?

concepts.label: Frame diagnosis
concepts.definition: Ordered investigation of activation, exact basis, actor capability, evidence, missing material distinctions, missing conjunction/translation, evaluation-family adequacy and need for another frame.

grounding.quote:
Whether a revision needs a new frame revision coordinate turns on the
frame's declarations; whether a result already closed stays valid is a
separate question. A revision is material when it changes a frame
declaration in a way that is material under
[FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology). A revision that changes no
declaration of the frame needs no new coordinate. That answer decides
nothing about any result: an unchanged declaration is no ground for
keeping a result closed.

concepts.label: Frame revision
concepts.definition: Revision of frame declarations or frame-set organisation, distinguished from reconsideration of closed-result validity. A material frame revision creates a new revision coordinate; a change to no frame declaration needs no new coordinate.

grounding.quote:
An actor receives one activated frame or one declared active frame
configuration, never an implied demand to reconstruct the complete
workspace from ambient context (P0). The minimum
activation packet contains:

concepts.label: Activation packet
concepts.definition: The actor's received activated frame or declared active frame configuration, with minimum identity/revision, evaluation/result algebra, exact subject/basis, material relations/invariants, authorities, admissible evidence/tools, capability/context envelope, exclusions/prohibited assumptions, dependencies/conjunction outputs, and invalidation/stop/reconfiguration conditions.

grounding.quote:
The following carrier-neutral content is sufficient to bind one declared
frame for one evaluation. It may be written in Markdown, structured data, a
prompt or another consumer-selected carrier without changing the relation
(P0, RF-016).

concepts.label: Minimal activation binding
concepts.definition: Carrier-neutral template sufficient to bind one declared frame for one evaluation: stable activation identity; declaration identity/revision and exact evaluation/closed algebra; exact subject or candidate and workspace/authority/dependency/configuration/time basis; material relations/invariants, source/semantic references, exclusions; actor/envelope; semantic/evaluation authority, material operation authority/subject/territory, decision/acceptance/publication authority; admissible evidence/acquisition, used dependency/overlap/input/conjunction/translation relations, result consumer/return; invalidation, stop, residual, re-entry and reconfiguration conditions.

grounding.quote:
The three carrier-neutral shapes below are the least content that declares
a frame, a frame set and an evaluation result. Each is sufficient as
written in Markdown or any other consumer-selected carrier (P0, P2;
RF-016).

concepts.label: Minimal declarations
concepts.definition: Three carrier-neutral shapes supply the least content declaring a frame, frame set and evaluation result, sufficient in Markdown or another consumer-selected carrier.

grounding.quote:
- result:
- inference relation:
- residual uncertainty:
- out_of_frame residual (missing relation or capability, owner, reconfiguration pressure):
- invalidation conditions:
- consuming decision or conjunction:

concepts.label: Minimal evaluation result
concepts.definition: Result record containing frame identity/revision, activation identity, evaluation, subject/basis, actor/envelope, semantic/evaluation/material operation/decision authorities, admissible evidence, result, inference relation, residual uncertainty, out_of_frame residual, invalidation conditions and consuming decision or conjunction.

grounding.quote: A declared decision rule consumes the closed results of several frames.

relations.meaning: Result conjunction consumes closed frame results; this consumption does not itself confer acceptance or authority.
conditions: Several frames have closed results and a declared decision rule consumes them.

grounding.quote:
The revision record lists those
results as reopened; a result leaves that list only by a recorded re-check
that finds it demonstrably independent of the change, or by re-evaluation
on the new revision.

relations.meaning: Material revision governs reopening of every prior-coordinate result, rather than selectively reopening only suspected dependents.
conditions: A frame has undergone material revision and a result binds its prior revision.
exceptions: Recorded re-check demonstrating independence or reevaluation on the new revision permits removal from the reopened list.

grounding.quote:
Coverage and evaluation results retain known uncertainty. Unresolved
relations, uncovered evaluations, contested evidence and unknown capability
stay explicit. Absence of a recorded counterexample is not evidence of
universal completeness (P4b, P6; open-world premise).

constraints.statement: Keep unresolved relations, uncovered evaluations, contested evidence and unknown capability explicit. No recorded counterexample does not establish universal completeness. Without an independently established closed-domain completeness predicate, inventory self-inspection cannot establish that no material evaluation is undiscovered; coverage stays falsifiable with a residual boundary.

grounding.quote: A refused activation performs no evaluation; `decision(holds)` assesses the composite predicate and is not its acceptance; a coverage status is a result of the audit, never of the covered evaluation, and an excluded row is met by its cited exclusion, never covered or performed

constraints.statement: Activation, conjunction, translation outcomes and coverage statuses answer their own predicates. Refused activation performs no evaluation; decision(holds) assesses a composite predicate rather than accepting it. Coverage audit status is not the covered evaluation's result. An excluded row is met by its cited exclusion, not covered or performed. Each refinement maps to one core value.
constraints.uncertainty: Full function outcome and coverage-status enumerations are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
each outcome below maps
to exactly one core value for the predicate its function names, the value
travels with that predicate and with the outcome, whose meaning stays here,
and an outcome named in the signatures above that would map to more than
one core value according to its cause carries the cause in its name, as in
`activation_refusal(basis)` (P5, P6). Purpose and material relation: a consumer that combines these
outcomes with other results reads them in the one core, so a refusal, a
conflict or a loss outside the accepted loss is neither mistaken for
success nor merged with an evaluation that was not performed.

constraints.statement: Each refined outcome carries its function's predicate and exactly one core value while retaining its local meaning; causes distinguish otherwise ambiguous outcome names. Refusal, conflict and unaccepted loss cannot mean success or be merged with an unperformed evaluation. Evaluate returns result, evidence and residuals under RF-012 and closed-result reuse under ACTIVATION §7; EVALUATION §7 qualifies all functions.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced core and qualification laws are not supplied in full.
conditions: Interpreting activate, conjoin or translate outcomes.

grounding.quote: | | `activation_refusal(basis)` | the subject or basis is stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched (RF-005), a topology mismatch included: the subject's topology is not the topology basis the frame declares (RF-011) | `invalid_basis` |

constraints.statement: activated_frame maps to satisfied when the declaration binds the exact evaluation, subject, basis and actor. activation_refusal(capability) maps to out_of_frame when a needed capability is declared by the frame but absent from the selected actor's declared envelope; it names the capability and its owner where supplied. activation_refusal(authority) maps to out_of_frame when needed semantic, evaluation, operation or decision authority is not admitted, naming its owner. activation_refusal(basis) maps to invalid_basis for stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched subject/basis, including topology mismatch. If no actor-usable frame declares a needed material relation or capability, activate directly returns out_of_frame. Activation answers activation only; refusal performs no evaluation.
conditions: Activating a frame for an evaluation, subject, basis and actor.

grounding.quote: | | `conflict` | the conjunction reports `falsified` while mandatory results for the same claim disagree, one `satisfied` and another `falsified`; the counterexample survives the join, and the disagreement stays unresolved for the decision authority | `falsified` |

constraints.statement: decision(holds) maps to satisfied when the core conjunction is satisfied. decision(fails) maps to falsified when the conjunction is falsified and no mandatory result for the same claim is satisfied. conflict also maps to falsified when mandatory results for the same claim include satisfied and falsified: its counterexample survives and disagreement remains unresolved for decision authority. indeterminate maps to indeterminate. Core out_of_frame or invalid_basis is returned directly, including basis mismatch, despite absent signature alternatives. Declared veto/deferral uses the outcome whose cause matches the core value or returns out_of_frame/invalid_basis directly. Planned assessments without closed results and required coverage without planned assessment are recorded beside the value, are not conjoin outcomes and map to no core value. decision(holds) is assessment, not acceptance.
constraints.uncertainty: The full core conjunction, veto and deferral laws are external.
conditions: Combining closed frame results under a declared decision rule.

grounding.quote: | | `refusal(basis)` | the source value or evidence binds a stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched basis or coordinate (RF-005) | `invalid_basis` |

constraints.statement: translated_value maps to satisfied when declared meaning is carried into target coordinates. declared_loss maps to satisfied only for loss inside declared accepted loss, carried as a residual. refusal(condition) maps to falsified for a declared refusal condition, loss outside accepted loss, or failed identity/equality under the declared equality law. refusal(authority) maps to out_of_frame when carried semantic/evaluation/operation/decision authority has a target-authority relation stated neither as preserved nor as a refusal condition, and names the owner. refusal(basis) maps to invalid_basis for stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched source basis/coordinate.
conditions: Translating a value or evidence into target coordinates.

grounding.quote:
They may overlap in subject, manifold or
evidence sources; neither evaluation consumes or influences the other's
unclosed working result.

constraints.statement: Separate activations return closed results. Subject, manifold and evidence sources may overlap, but neither evaluation may consume or influence the other's unclosed working result.
conditions: Several frames independently evaluate the same subject.

grounding.quote:
where the
translation is represented in `a_c` it is recorded in the preservation,
introduced, removed and residual fields of
[AC-013](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-013-transformation). This section adds
only the frame fields: the source and target coordinates, the
provenance, the equality law and the refusal conditions.

constraints.statement: Declare source/target coordinates, preserved meaning, accepted loss, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions. ACTIVATION §4 Refinement owns what preservation/loss must show and the licensing law. When represented in a_c, record preservation, introduced, removed and residual fields under AC-013; this frame section adds only coordinates, provenance, equality law and refusal conditions.
constraints.uncertainty: External refinement and transformation requirements are not supplied.
conditions: A frame supplies evidence or value consumed inside another.

constraints.statement: No frame relation supplies a default universal topology. Declare only relations needed by evaluations and coverage claims. A possible future interaction does not require general composition law in every frame; governing/subordinate inheritance requires a real declared authority or decomposition relation.

grounding.quote:
Changing any material member may invalidate the
coverage result; whether a change does is decided by
[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse): it does when it
could change that result, as a material input change or a changed basis
(P3, P6).

constraints.statement: Tuple change may invalidate coverage; under the referenced reuse rule it does when the change could alter the result as a material input change or changed basis.
conditions: A material member of the coverage tuple changes.

grounding.quote:
The inventory records provenance and
materiality. Artifact presence, file count, operation count, test count or
repository reachability proves no evaluation coverage (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Derive inventory from every material available source, including goals/intent/product/requirements/accepted method; accepted design with ontology, identities, lifecycles, authorities and algorithms; implementation capabilities and observable behaviour; operational/release/security/safety/governance obligations; direct/indirect dependencies and seams; evidence/tests/scenarios/qualification/acceptance claims; tickets/check-ins/commentary/post-mortems/incidents/rejected candidates; long loops/resets/repeated repairs/rival paths; known capability limits/prior invisible violations; and applicable external law/contracts/standards. Record provenance and materiality. Artifact presence, file/operation/test counts and repository reachability establish no evaluation coverage.
conditions: Sources are available and material; enumerated kinds apply where applicable.

grounding.quote: | operation authority | the existing owner grant for construction, transformation, admission, publication or mutation where the evaluation performs one; otherwise none |

constraints.statement: Ledger minimum: exact evaluation predicate; materiality provenance; exact subject/basis coordinate; capable selected frames; required actor competence/context; semantic owner; existing operation grant when construction/transformation/admission/publication/mutation occurs, otherwise none; decision owner; required observations/provenance; material frame/seam dependencies; status; uncertainty/exclusion/re-entry residual. covered → satisfied for capable evaluation on tuple without conflict; separately_covered → satisfied for separately activated frames each evaluating without conflict; excluded_by_authority → satisfied for cited governing exclusion; conditionally_covered → indeterminate when its condition is unestablished, naming condition and deciding evidence in residual; conflicted → falsified for unresolved covering frame/result/authority conflict, retaining its counterexample for decision authority; uncovered → falsified for absent capable evaluation and absent cited exclusion, that absence being counterexample; unknown → indeterminate when admissible evidence cannot decide coverage, including unknown capability or materiality.
conditions: For each evaluation.

grounding.quote:
Where the coverage tuple itself is stale, advanced,
ambiguous or mismatched, the audit returns `invalid_basis` (RF-005) and
assigns no status.

constraints.statement: Status/core values answer the audit coverage-obligation predicate, never the evaluated claim. Satisfied exclusion establishes obligation met by exclusion, not evaluation coverage or performance. In conjunction over the governed claim, an uncovered row denotes required coverage without a planned assessment, not a falsified component. A stale, advanced, ambiguous or mismatched tuple yields invalid_basis with no status. Conditional, conflicted, unknown and uncovered rows are not covered; cited exclusion is not failure.

grounding.quote:
Evaluation-row coverage is insufficient when two covered relations interact
in a way capable of changing the governed outcome. Every material
interaction is covered by one frame, a declared conjunction, a translation
or a material composition evaluation (P4a, P2).

constraints.statement: Evaluation-row coverage alone is insufficient. Every material interaction requires coverage by one frame, declared conjunction, translation or material-composition evaluation.
conditions: Two covered relations interact in a way capable of changing the governed outcome.

grounding.quote:
Every material evaluation identifies semantic and decision authority.
Every material operation also identifies its existing construction,
transformation, admission, publication or mutation authority. A frame set
with broad observational reach, an unresolved decision owner or an
effectful path without operation authority is not closed (P6).

constraints.statement: Every material evaluation identifies semantic and decision authority; every material operation identifies its existing construction/transformation/admission/publication/mutation authority. Broad observational reach does not establish closure; unresolved decision ownership or an effectful path lacking operation authority prevents closure.
constraints.uncertainty: The source's compressed list includes broad observational reach alongside closure defects; read with the explicit authority requirements rather than as a prohibition on broad observation.
conditions: Material evaluations or operations are present.

grounding.quote:
Coverage includes known success, refusal, boundary, integration, recovery,
reconstruction and competing-path cases where they are material.
Historical failures stay first-class coverage inputs until a declared frame
detects or excludes their recurrence (P4b, P5).

constraints.statement: Include known success, refusal, boundary, integration, recovery, reconstruction and competing-path cases. Historical failures remain first-class coverage inputs until declared detection or exclusion of recurrence.
conditions: Cases are material.
exceptions: A historical failure ceases to require this retained input treatment when a declared frame detects or excludes its recurrence.

grounding.quote:
Human authority may require independently activated frame coverage for
evaluations whose failure has high consequence, weak observability, strong
confirmation bias or a history of local proof masking. Such coverage uses a
separately activated evaluation relation and declares any additional
assurance-independence conditions. A persona label alone establishes
neither relation (P6).

constraints.statement: Human authority may impose independently activated coverage; risk characteristics do not themselves automatically impose it. Required coverage uses separate activation and declares additional assurance-independence conditions. A persona label alone establishes neither relation.
conditions: Human authority requires independent coverage for failures with high consequence, weak observability, strong confirmation bias or historical local proof masking.

grounding.quote:
Operational full coverage is relative to its tuple. It is not a claim that
no undiscovered evaluation exists (P6; P0 with the open-world premise).

constraints.statement: Require: every known material evaluation covered by at least one capable frame; every material interaction with declared evaluation/conjunction/translation/composition; every evaluation with semantic and decision authority and every material operation with inherited operation authority; every mandatory claim with admissible evidence and refusal paths; required independently activated overlaps and assurance-independence conditions present; no unresolved frame-result conflict hidden by aggregation; exclusions citing governing authority; uncovered/unknown residuals explicit and compatible with the claim. Coverage remains tuple-relative and asserts no absence of undiscovered evaluations.
constraints.uncertainty: How universal coverage of known material evaluations accommodates exclusions and compatible uncovered residuals is not fully specified here.
conditions: Claiming operational full coverage for the declared tuple.

grounding.quote:
Without an independently established closed-domain completeness predicate,
a finite frame set cannot establish the absence of every undiscovered
material evaluation by inspecting its own declared inventory. A finite,
formally closed domain may support exhaustive coverage relative to that
domain and its completeness predicate; the result does not generalise
beyond that boundary. Formal incompleteness results motivate this caution;
they do not by themselves prove that a particular workspace or frame set is
incomplete (P0 with the open-world premise; P6).

constraints.statement: A finite inventory cannot self-establish absence of all undiscovered material evaluations without an independently established closed-domain completeness predicate. Exhaustive results stay within that domain; formal incompleteness results alone prove no particular workspace incomplete. Coverage remains falsifiable and externally challengeable through outside human knowledge, independent review, historical failures/predecessors, mutation/adversarial/counterexample search, live operation/user behaviour, adjacent-domain comparison and changed capability/law/dependencies/topology. Explicit residual boundary is required; metaphysical or universal completeness claims are forbidden.
exceptions: An independently established closed-domain completeness predicate may support exhaustive coverage within a finite formally closed domain.

grounding.quote: These observations trigger frame diagnosis (P4b, P5):

constraints.statement: Trigger diagnosis for: a competent actor repeatedly missing a known material violation; local repair creating/duplicating another authority path; repeated resets after apparently valid local completion; long implementation loops without stable closure; passing proof with unbound claimed outcome; material failure visible only after broad integration; repeated context expansion without decidable question; same frame name used for different material relations; or topology mutation leaving prior verdicts apparently current. These signals trigger diagnosis, not an automatic new frame.
conditions: Any listed observation occurs.

grounding.quote:
Question 1 is answered by family inclusion, not by set membership. An
evaluation is within a frame's family when the question it decides is one
the frame's declared evaluation family states, at the frame's declared
coordinates (RF-001). Membership of the frame in the frame set, the frame's
name, a role label or similar wording of the question does not place an
evaluation in the frame's family; an activation of a frame on an evaluation
outside its family answers question 1 no, whatever the frame's standing in
the set (P2, the evaluations determine the attention surface; P1, a name
carries no meaning; the material relation drawn is evaluation-to-family
inclusion).

constraints.statement: Use the eight diagnosis questions in the declared order. Correct activation requires the decided question to belong to the declared evaluation family at declared coordinates. Frame-set membership, frame name, role label and similar wording do not establish inclusion. Activation outside the family answers the first question no regardless of frame standing. The order prevents difficulty alone from creating another frame.
conditions: Determining whether the correct frame was activated.

grounding.quote:
Every prior closed result bound to the previous
revision of a materially revised frame is bound to a mismatched coordinate
(RF-005) and is invalidated for reuse until it is re-checked against the
new revision (RF-011; ACTIVATION §7). The revision record lists those
results as reopened; a result leaves that list only by a recorded re-check
that finds it demonstrably independent of the change, or by re-evaluation
on the new revision. A material revision does not select which of the
results bound to the prior revision it reopens, and silence does not keep
a result closed (P3, P4b).

constraints.statement: Every material revision changes frame identity/revision coordinates and states which activations, results and coverage claims require reevaluation. Every closed result bound to the materially revised frame's prior revision is invalid for reuse and listed reopened, without selective omission or preservation by silence. Unchanged declarations do not preserve result validity: ACTIVATION §7 may reopen results without revision, recorded in work state. Discovery of outside-family activation or newly acquired material admissible evidence reopens the result and every consuming ledger row/coverage claim, preserving demonstrably independent survivors. Even harmless clarification leaves reuse subject to the consumer's exact applicability check.

conditions: Material frame revision or a change relevant to closed-result reuse.
exceptions: A recorded re-check demonstrates independence, or re-evaluation occurs on the new revision.
